correctness.rationale: The entire frozen classification proof was independently reconstructed. The defect-one identity yields exactly four cases. A singleton overlap forces a double star using interval connectivity and relative down/up closure. A singleton outside the union forces three elements. One nonmaximal element with singleton lower interval forces the complete two-bottom bipartite poset by the upper cover boundary; the last case is dual. Conversely the displayed pairs have union P and exact extremal boundaries, hence are saturated. Distinct-family counts are 3,5,n+2 with the stated small-size overlaps. Complete primary definitions of intervals, relative boundaries and W were read, together with Proposition6.1 proof, Theorems6.3/6.5, Corollaries6.6/6.7 and their proofs. They have exactly the quoted hypotheses, saturated-pair weight and normalization. Imported homological theorems are credited Aoki, not reproved as new here.

value.rationale: This classifies every connected extremizer of a natural sharp homological bound, over every coefficient field, and enumerates the isomorphism types. It is a structural equality theorem rather than an arbitrary finite database slice.

final_claim: A connected \(n\)-element poset attains \(\operatorname{gldim}\Lambda_P=n-1\) exactly for the double stars \(D_{a,b}\) and the two complete height-two families \(K_{2,n-2}\), \(K_{n-2,2}\), equivalently attaining interval-resolution global dimension \(n-3\).
